fill.best_season: Late July through September, once the slopes above Nada Lake are snow-free
fill.overview: A little-visited high ridge in the eastern Enchantments, rising north of the Nada Lake basin between Tamarack Meadows and Toketie Creek. The way in is the long Snow Lakes trail, then off-trail up a steep buttress and basin to the ridge crest, where a string of rocky knobs leads to the high point. Quiet, with no crowds and no trail past the lake.
fill.beta: From Nada Lake, leave the trail at the west shore and work up the slope beside the outlet falls to the upper basin. Continue to the saddle on the ridge, then follow the crest over a series of knobs. The first tower is not the highest; keep going along the crest to the true summit, passing a few boulder moves and a slot.
fill.approach: Start at the Snow Lakes Trailhead on Icicle Creek Road and hike the Snow Lakes trail past Lake Viviane to Nada Lake (roughly 5 to 6 miles). Beyond the end of the maintained trail, climb the buttress ramp above the lake outlet into the upper basin, then head to the ridge saddle.
fill.descent_text: Return the way you came along the crest and down to the basin, then drop back to Nada Lake and the Snow Lakes trail. In snow season the descent side can be poor, so a different line should be chosen with care.
fill.turnaround: Turn back if the slope above Nada Lake is still snow-covered and steep without axe and crampons, or if the afternoon sun is softening the snow.
fill.bail: Retreat down the buttress ramp to Nada Lake and the trail.
what_to_bring: Ice axe and crampons (June or any early-season attempt)
hazards: Steep, loose ground and cliffs on the buttress above Nada Lake
Very long day with a large amount of gain
Rocky, exposed knobs along the crest
watch_out: Wilderness overnight permits are required for camping in the core zone from mid-May to October
Hot, shadeless slopes in July and August
pro_tips: Camp near the lakes in Tamarack Meadows to turn the long hike into a short summit day (permit needed).
The trail ends at the west shore of Nada Lake, so be ready to find your own way from there.
features: Views of The Temple and the Stuart Range
